We need a retrosynthesis route with 1 reaction (single step) to target molecule. The guidance describes carbonyl-ene reaction forward: a ketone + alkene -> product with new C-C bond, forming hydroxyl and five-membered ring. So retrosynthetic direction: break the product into a ketone precursor and an alkene precursor that undergo carbonyl-ene to give product.

Our target: looks like a bicyclic? Let's parse: [CH2]=[C]([c]1... aromatic) attached to chiral carbon bearing a cyclopentanol with CF3? Actually [C@@H]1[CH2][CH2][CH2][C@@]1([OH])... That's a cyclopentanol fused? The product likely formed from a cyclopentanone (ketone) undergoing ene with an alkene (maybe exocyclic double bond attached to aromatic). So retrosynthetic step: disconnect the C-C bond formed between the carbonyl carbon (of cyclopentanone) and the alkene carbon (the exocyclic double bond). Also the C=O becomes C-OH.

Thus precursor: a cyclopentanone with CF3 at carbon adjacent? The product has CF3 attached to carbon 15 (C:15) which is attached to the same carbon as the OH? Actually [C@@:13]1([OH:14])[C:15]([F:16])([F:17])[F:18] indicates carbon 13 is part of ring, bearing OH, and attached to carbon 15 which is CF3 group (C with three Fs). So precursor likely cyclopentanone with CF3 substituent at alpha carbon? The carbonyl carbon becomes carbon 13 after reaction? In ene, carbonyl carbon becomes alcohol after addition, so carbonyl carbon is the carbon bearing OH in product. So precursor: cyclopentanone (C=O) at that carbon, with CF3 attached to adjacent carbon (maybe same carbon?). In product, CF3 attached to carbon 15 which is attached to carbon 13 (the carbon bearing OH). So in precursor, carbon 13 is carbonyl carbon, carbon 15 is attached to carbonyl carbon (alpha carbon) as CF3 substituent. So precursor: a cyclopentanone with CF3 at alpha position (i.e., alpha-CF3 cyclopentanone). The other fragment: an alkene (maybe styrene-like) that attaches to carbonyl carbon via ene. The alkene is CH2= C( aromatic )? The product has exocyclic double bond attached to carbon 2 which is attached to aromatic ring. That double bond becomes single bond after reaction, connecting carbon 2 to carbonyl carbon (13). So precursor alkene: CH2= C( aromatic ) (i.e., a styrene derivative). So overall retrosynthesis: target -> precursors: (1) alpha-CF3 cyclopentanone (with appropriate stereochemistry) and (2) 1-phenyl-ethylene (styrene) maybe with substituents? The aromatic ring is phenyl (c1ccccc1). So alkene is CH2= C(Ph). That's styrene.

Thus we need to find a template for carbonyl-ene reaction. Search for template with functional_groups_broken: ["ketones","C-C double bonds"] and formed: ["aliphatic hydroxyls","five-membered rings"]. Already attempted but got empty. Maybe need different criteria: functional_groups_broken: ["ketones"], bonds_broken: ["C=O"], functional_groups_formed: ["aliphatic hydroxyls"], bonds_formed: ["C-O"]? But we can try search without bonds.
